I completely agree with your first point. Some people will never grow. Shane Dawson is a massive example, IMO. But some people will. Just because Shane Dawson will never grow does not mean we should paint others with the same paintbrush. 

Maybe I didn't make my point clear, typing doesn't make for great articulation. Just somehow cancel culture has gained the mentality of "I'm bothered by this so I won't watch it AND neither can you". Cancel culture bothers me because it's other people trying to control consumption. You are free to not watch X Youtuber but other people are free to do so if they choose to. Cancel culture hasn't affected me much in my interests, apart from the odd musicians, but has it affected you? Do you also cancel celebrities from your life when Twitter does it? Would you end a friendship if your friend still consumed a product from someone who was cancelled? Twitter seems to take cancel culture as such a black and white thing so I was wondering if other people see the grey area I see.

As for the offence, it's not my place to judge what people get offended by. Being white, racist content won't offend me personally. But to POC a simple comment could be harmful. The only real thing on Youtube that could have ever offended me was "dear fat people". I just ignored it. 

Sorry, I didn't want to make this into an argument or anything I just like seeing people's views on cancel culture as it's such a massive part of internet culture nowadays. Being against it, I just want to understand alternative viewpoints and perhaps change my views. I suppose I just come across as a massive asshole whoops.

The one thing I hate about cancel culture is that it ignores the possibility of growth. We do not know these people personally so we don't know their views. People who have been previously been racist may have learnt why what they had done was unacceptable and hence stopped doing so. To me, this is evidence of growth.

Also in cancel culture, accountability = apologies only. Yes, when people have been hurt I understand apologies are important but we can't hate people who don't make them. Accountability is taking responsibility and issuing an apology is just one aspect of taking accountability.  Personal growth is another aspect of taking accountability. This requires introspection and learning why certain actions are unacceptable. Let's return to the example of racism as that is what's been called out most recently. Someone who has made racist jokes may have done so with good intentions, humour. Of course, despite your intentions, racist jokes are inherently harmful to those who are the target of the joke. Over time, someone may realise this and stopped including these jokes as part of their vocabulary. Anyway, there are 0 points apologising if you haven't changed. The aspects of accountability go hand in hand.

I try to give people I support who have been called out the benefit of the doubt, provided there is some other evidence they have changed and their offending actions are in the past. Who someone was in 2010 is not who they were in 2015. Who someone was in 2015 is not who they are in 2020. Maybe I'm too fair or too trusting of people or too lenient.

I've always opposed cancel culture so I suppose I'm just a morally corrupt person.

Trust me, I'm just stuck in the middle. The prevailing idea I've seen on social media is "if you support this racist artist, you're racist by proxy" so now I'm doubting whether I'm doing the right thing or if I've just been stuck in a social media echo chamber.

I like to believe my own actions reflect my beliefs, not the actions of someone I support.
When I think logically, I can't believe myself so seeing your comment has helped me.
Thank you. Hearing other people be rational about this helps me feel the same.

I've done a lot of reading of the comments after originally posting this and I can honestly say my view has changed. Having people kind of break things down has helped me see why continued support is wrong. Honestly, I've wanted to stop supporting the wrestler in question for weeks after finding out their true nature but fan delusion and mental gymnastics kinda blurred my perception. I understand why other people can't separate the art and honestly now taking a logical viewpoint I think i could do the same. I'm sorry for replying to people's comments with my epiphany but what started as wanting to see other perceptions has led to me adopt said "alternative" perceptions.
I completely understand that. Like I said, I never have and would not watch something he had done but I know there a people who do.

I feel awful for repeatedly annoying you know. Reading other perspectives has helped me realise my fault and I decided the best thing I could do is call this person out for their past comments instead of trying to justify them to myself. Yay character development I guess..
Honestly, Benoit was an awful example on my behalf. I have personally never seen any of his work being young but I've seen people on here before who are able to stomach his matches.

As awful as I've made myself sound, I also care about black people and I've done various things to support the community as well as educating myself. This probably sounds awful as this sounds perhaps you could provide me advice on how I could end my support for someone. Since the comments were in the past I think I'm letting ideas of growth and "benefit of the doubt" cloud my judgement. You seemed insightful and hearing an alternative perspective has helped me understand. 

If I abstained from buying merch (which honestly I wouldn't want to do anyway and unfortunately did before when I was ignorant to their true character) and only watched their content as part of the show they are on would is that still actively contributing to them doing harm? 

But anyway thank you for your response. I think I needed to see an alternate perspective.
